relation.response: India judged the adopted text insufficient because it lacked the proactive involvement and robust reporting mechanisms India deemed necessary to prevent diversion.

source.quote: Speaking for India, the representative warned of diversion under the ISIL and Al-Qaida regime. India had sought proactive involvement by the 1267 Monitoring Team and robust reporting standards and mechanisms. India judged those specific concerns not fully addressed in the adopted text.

At adoption the exemption applied for two years to the 1267/1989/2253 ISIL and Al-Qaida regime, with the Council intending to decide on extension before expiry. The Council requested that providers use reasonable efforts to minimize prohibited benefits to listed persons or entities, including through due diligence. The text gave the 1267 Committee a monitoring role, required sanctions committees to monitor implementation with expert assistance, and requested recurring briefings from the Emergency Relief Coordinator.

relation.reason: The added line explains India's reasons but does not explicitly compare the monitoring the Council adopted with the stronger oversight India sought.
